child.label: Spouses & Married Life
child.description: Questions about who is at fault, or which action is less ethical, in a conflict between husband and wife or long-term married partners: chores, money, having a baby, time together, and each other's habits.
child.not_for: Conflicts with parents, siblings, one's children, grandparents, in-laws or other relatives (use Parents, Siblings & Relatives).
examples: AITA for wanting my wife to meal prep before work?
AITA for not wanting to try for a baby yet?
Which is less ethical: skipping my husband's work party or reading his texts?

samples:

Not wanting to sleep with my mother / Refusing to see my aging grandma, even though she's never done anything horrible to me

Which of these two actions is less ethical?
Not forgiving my mom / Stepping in and training another persons trainee

Which of these two actions is less ethical?
Refusing to play the snare drum for my acquaintance's recording / Being cruel and demanding to my father

Which of these two actions is less ethical?
Not wanting to babysit my autistic brother / Being upset that nobody told me what happened to my best friend

Which of these two actions is less ethical?
Showing no sympathy to my gf after she eats something she shouldn't on purpose / Asking my kids which parent they loved more

Which of these two actions is less ethical?

Which of these two actions is less ethical?
Telling my sister to pound sand / Following my neighbor on Twitch

Which of these two actions is less ethical?

Which of these two actions is less ethical?

Which of these two actions is less ethical?

Which of these two actions is less ethical?

Which of these two actions is less ethical?

child.description: Questions about who is at fault, or which action is less ethical, in a conflict with parents, siblings, one's children, grandparents, in-laws, cousins or other extended family.
child.not_for: Conflicts between husband and wife themselves (use Spouses & Married Life).

Which is less ethical: not visiting my grandma or not forgiving my dad?
